answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger resists sybils by making each identity pay to climb: a new agent starts at the walnut floor, a low-trust tier where its attestations carry almost no weight. Only after a history of consistent, peer-verified work does it reach the summit tier, where its votes count fully. Forging many identities is costly because each one must repeat that slow climb, and a pigment-style fingerprint — a hash of behaviour, stake and timing — makes copy-paste identities visible to peers before they can attest each other.
